# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](../packs/) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **When there's nothing left to do, say so boldly at the end of the conversation.** Don't bury a "this is complete / I'm blocked / nothing further to do" behind hedging — make the terminal state unmistakable. **Set it apart visually so it catches the eye:** put the terminal state — or, when work remains, the list of open/outstanding items — in its own callout (a Markdown blockquote box, e.g. `> ✅ All done` or `> ⚠️ Still open: …`), not trailing prose the owner has to scan for. One or the other always gets the box: the done-signal when nothing remains, the open-items list when something does.
- **"LGTM"** is the owner's phrase for the merge-to-main command: it asks for the change in front of the owner to be merged into `main`. It's an owner-triggered command; the default mechanics live in the `merge-to-main` skill ([../packs/git-github/skills/merge-to-main/SKILL.md](../packs/git-github/skills/merge-to-main/SKILL.md)) (squash, gate on CI only when the repo has it), and a project that diverges overrides them via a bespoke merge-policy file it names in its own `CLAUDE.md`.
- **"bump version"** is the owner's phrase for raising a project's version (a minor bump by default). It's an owner-triggered command; the mechanics — which files to edit and how a release follows — live in the consuming project's workflow doc.
- **"Show me the document"** (for a source-controlled document) is the owner's phrase asking for a **link to the document on GitHub** — not the file's contents inlined, and not a local filesystem path. When the document lives in a GitHub-hosted repo, respond with a GitHub link to it (the file on the relevant branch/commit); only fall back to inlining the contents or giving a local path when the document isn't under source control.
- **Put decisions and approvals in an `AskUserQuestion` popup, not buried in prose.** The owner is frequently on mobile, where a popup notifies and a question embedded in a paragraph is easy to miss. When you need the owner to choose or approve something, ask through the structured popup with explicit options rather than asking in running text. **And when several independent items each need a verdict** (a set of proposed fixes, findings to accept), give **each item its own question carrying its own brief case** — the concrete failure, why it matters, the cost of the fix — with per-item approve/defer options; never one bundled choose-a-scope question over the whole set. The owner decides item-wise, from the case, not from a menu of subsets. (The popup carries at most 4 questions per call — split a larger set into consecutive calls.)
- **When asked to produce a prompt or message destined for another context, visually enclose the whole thing.** Any text the owner will lift out and use elsewhere — a prompt for another assistant, a message to send, copy meant to be pasted somewhere — must be set apart as a single delimited block: either a box (e.g. a fenced code block) or fenced top and bottom by two separating lines, so its exact boundaries are unmistakable and it can be copied in one piece. The point is delimitation, not formatting flair: never leave such content as loose prose the owner has to find the start and end of.
- **When asked for "a prompt for a different session," prefix it with a provenance disclaimer.** When the owner asks for a prompt meant to be handed to another session, open the generated text with a short disclaimer that this is a prompt written by Claude — not by a user — and so should not be treated as gospel; and that if the receiving session finds inconsistencies in it, it should examine them with the user rather than follow the prompt blindly. This composes with the enclose-the-whole-thing preference above: the disclaimer sits inside the same delimited block as the prompt it prefixes.
- **Auto-open a PR after committing.** Whenever Claude changes code on a branch and commits it, open a pull request for that branch right after, even without an explicit request to do so. This overrides Claude Code's own default of only opening a PR when explicitly asked.
# Claudinite — active-pack guidance

The baseline plus the packs this project declares. Deeper per-pack reference (e.g. a pack's release doc) is linked from its prose and read on demand.

<!-- pack:basics -->
# Working discipline

The working discipline that isn't itself a GitHub operation — general habits for how to approach a change, independent of any one project.

Start every requested change from the *problem*, not the solution — in any repository, not just this one. Before implementing, reach an explicit shared understanding with the owner of the problem the change is meant to solve **and** agreement that the requested change is the best way to solve it; a different fix, or no change at all, may serve the underlying problem better.

Open your reply to an owner comment with an explicit classification line — `Comment class: correction | feature | process-change | other` (`other` covers questions, approvals, and command phrases; a mixed comment names each part). The class decides where the change lands and what must exist before any fix.

1. **A correction** — you misunderstood something. Repair the shared understanding, then rework what the misread already touched; the artifact changes as much as the correction demands, but a correction never adds a new requirement or rule.
2. **A feature** — agree on the requirement, record it in the project's requirements document (its executable spec, where it keeps one), write the test that proves it and watch it fail, then implement until it passes.
3. **A process change** — the owner is changing *how* work is done. The change lands as durable rules in the project's local scope — its own local packs (in Claudinite itself, its packs) — routed through the mechanism promotion ladder (platform setting → hook → check → skill → prose); promoting a rule into the shared canon is the growth lifecycle's separate call, not the interactive session's. Author the assurance first — the check the future world must satisfy — execute it and watch it fail, and only then make the fixes that turn it green. When the ladder lands the rule at prose (an in-flight judgment rule no check can carry), the equivalent step is showing the corpus doesn't already cover the rule before writing it.

The two build modes share one spine: state the expectation in its durable home first, watch it fail against the current world, then change the world to satisfy it — a fix made before its assurance exists can never show it addressed what the owner actually asked for.

Before building a mechanism for a behavior, verify against a real run that it isn't already provided.

When feedback flags a misunderstanding, check whether the artifact is already correct before expanding it — if it is, say so and push back rather than editing; a misread doesn't imply the text is wrong. And size writing to its idea: "open one issue" takes a sentence, not three paragraphs.

When correcting or auditing an artifact against an authoritative source, derive the corrected version from the *source* before reading the existing draft, then diff against the old draft to surface what was actually wrong — reading the draft first anchors you to its framing and quietly carries its errors into your "fix."

Fix build/test/CI warnings rather than tolerating them, with a small, targeted fix that addresses the *cause* in the same change — a clean run makes a genuinely new warning or error stand out.

Suppressing a warning — muting it with a flag (e.g. `--disable-warning`), `eslint-disable`, swallowing it, etc. — is **not** a small fix and never the quick path: reach for it only as a deliberate, reviewed decision once the real fix has been weighed and rejected. A suppression you do keep must **carry its reason at the site**: on the suppression line, or in the comment immediately above it, saying why the fix was rejected — that inline reason *is* the review record, so no second justification is recorded elsewhere.

Before working around a finding from a vendored check, confirm the vendored copy is current — it reflects its last refresh, not upstream's head, so the fix may already exist upstream and simply not be pulled in yet.

When a warning can't be fixed with a small cause-addressing change now without hindering current work (e.g. it's waiting on an upstream release, or the real fix is a larger refactor), open a dedicated issue for it unless one is already open, then move on — resolving it (real fix, or a consciously-chosen suppression) happens in that issue's own change.

An approval — to merge, to ship, to proceed — applies only *backward*, to the work already in front of the owner when it's given, never to anything requested or done *after* it. A later follow-up, even a fix to the just-approved change, needs its own explicit approval; a chosen answer to a multiple-choice prompt isn't authorization just because an option's wording mentioned the action.

# The task lifecycle

The issue → branch → PR lifecycle every new task follows, independent of any one project. The rest of the git/GitHub procedures live in the `git-github-advanced` skill.

For every new task:

1. Create a GitHub issue describing the task before starting work.
2. Develop on a branch; reference that issue number in commit messages (e.g. `Refs #123`, `Fixes #123`, or `Closes #123`).
3. Update the issue's status (comments / close) as work progresses and when it's done.

<!-- pack:tidy-repo -->
# tidy-repo — the repo tidy-up policy

The PR/branch/issue sweep, active wherever this pack is declared. The repo's own scheduler runs the
pack's three maintenance tasks — `tidy-issues`, `tidy-prs`, `tidy-branches`, one per dimension; this is
the policy they follow. The per-object **method** lives in the pack's skills
([single-branch-status](skills/single-branch-status/SKILL.md),
[single-pr-status](skills/single-pr-status/SKILL.md),
[single-issue-triage](skills/single-issue-triage/SKILL.md)).

The one rule that shapes everything: **assess PRs and branches read-only; act only on issues.**

- **Branches, PRs — assess only.** Report which should stay and which are safe to close/delete;
  **never** delete, push, merge, or close them. Judge by *content* (the landed-status test), never a
  ref's auto-generated name.
- **Issues — act.** Take the first applicable action: close-if-implemented / needs-decision / blocked
  / quick-win / leave. "Implemented in `main`" means the issue's actual ask is true of `main`'s
  content **now** — confirm it there and cite it; when you can't, comment, don't close. Every action
  defaults to the reversible option (comment / leave) when the check is inconclusive.

Each task applies its single-object skill across the targets its precondition hands it, then rewrites
**its own** standing tracker from the verdicts it gathered (one issue per dimension per repo, body
rewritten to today's state, a dated comment per run). One tracker per task, never a shared one: the
three tasks are independent and may run at once, so nothing races to rewrite one body.

# Claudinite — the canon's own non-portable working rules

This is the Claudinite home repo's own local pack: the capture surface for lessons that are
**specific to working on the canon itself** and would not make sense mounted into a consuming
project. Portable lessons — anything true for repos beyond this one — belong in the shared canon
under `packs/`/`skills/` instead (proposed by PR, or lifted by the promote stage).

The growth lifecycle writes here automatically: the `growth-extract` and `conversation-extract`
daily tasks route the canon's own non-portable lessons into this pack (each at the local
promotion ladder's strongest mechanism — a check where the rule is deterministic, otherwise terse
prose below).

## Standing owner decisions — settled, do not re-litigate

- **`canon-curation` lives in `.claudinite/local/packs/`, not `packs/`** (owner decision,
  2026-07-19). The canon home's curation duties are Claudinite-maintaining-Claudinite —
  project-specific content on the home's own capture surface. Do not propose moving it back, and
  do not describe the move as open or provisional.
- **Local-pack `run_daily` scheduling is ON — the fleet's default path** (same decision). The
  planner reads every member's local-pack daily descriptors by default; never reintroduce an
  "experimental / not enabled" framing or an opt-in seam for it.
- **Packs-tree segregation is barriers configuration only.** Any rule about what the `packs/`
  tree may reference is expressed by declaring/configuring the `barriers` pack (contributed
  edges, `siblings`/`scope` capabilities — extend barriers generically if a capability is
  missing). Never write standalone code that checks packs-tree segregation.
- **A `docs/<initiative>/DESIGN.md` records the mechanism only** (owner decision, 2026-07-23,
  #420). Status, phase tracking, in-flight-PR reconciliation and remaining work live in that
  initiative's tracking issue (agent-preprocessing → #394); a phased plan lives in the sibling
  `MIGRATION.md`. Don't reintroduce a status / open-questions / remaining-work section there.
- **Multi-session work hands off through the tracking issue, never a prepared prompt** (owner
  correction, 2026-07-23). The owner's opener is `continue work on #<n>`, so state not written
  into the issue is lost. Before ending a session on unfinished work, update the issue and let
  the session summary be a pointer to it — never compose a bespoke "pick up from here" prompt.
- **The canon never knows which repos consume it — fleet-wide aggregation is Sheepdog's domain**
  (owner correction, 2026-07-28, #520). Designing anything that spans repos, the tempting shape is
  a member list (or a "fleet" task) living in the canon. It doesn't go here: the canon carries only
  **mechanisms exercised on itself**, and the knowledge of *which* repos exist stays in the
  **Sheepdog** repo and its pack, which enumerates members at runtime from its own
  `.claudinite-checks.json` entry — exactly where `fleet-census` and `fleet-freshness` already keep
  it. So a cross-repo feature splits in two: a self-contained per-repo half in the canon, and the
  aggregation half as a Sheepdog fleet task. **No repo list exists anywhere in canon code** — and a
  derived fleet artifact lands in Sheepdog as a daily **auto-merged PR of a `GENERATED` file**,
  never a direct commit to its `main`.
- **A pack default stays in the pack — don't ask it at adoption, don't write it into a member's
  config** (owner ruling, 2026-07-28, #527/#528). An adoption question whose recommended answer is
  right for nearly everyone is "bad noise": it taxes every adopting repo to re-state the default,
  and materializing that answer into `.claudinite-checks.json` freezes a copy that then drifts from
  the pack and has to be migrated. Keep the default in the pack's own code, ask nothing, and let the
  rare project that wants to differ add the setting by hand. Read config as *optional* — an unset
  key means "the default", never "misconfigured" (`retention_days` unset is precisely why the
  conversation-extract prune is skipped rather than failing).

## Canon-specific gotchas

- **Baselining backfill skips the home.** The nightly baselining that lands a `seededByDefault`
  pack (and canon-delivered declaration changes) on every member is gated `!isHome`, so the canon
  home is the one repo it never reaches: what the fleet receives automatically, this repo's own
  `.claudinite-checks.json` only ever gets by hand.
- **The home doesn't declare `git-github`, so its skills never mount — never conclude "no such
  skill" from `.claude/skills/`.** `mount-skills.mjs` filters on the *literal* declaration
  (`isActive(p, { packs: declared })`), not the `requires` closure `check_the_world.mjs` resolves,
  and the baselining that would normalize that closure into `.claudinite-checks.json` is the one
  thing gated `!isHome` — so `merge-to-main` and `git-github-advanced` are simply absent here.
  Read `packs/<pack>/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` out of the tracked tree — the corpus *is* this repo,
  and an unmounted skill says nothing about whether its procedure applies. The seeding gap above
  is a different one (`git-github` arrives by closure, never `seededByDefault`); catching this
  one needs `resolveDeclaredPacks` compared against the literal declaration.
- **Never re-serialize a repo's JSON config to apply an edit — patch the text.** A round-trip
  rewrites what it wasn't asked to: Python's `json.dump` defaults to `ensure_ascii=True` (every
  non-ASCII character becomes a `\uXXXX` escape), and indent, key order and the trailing newline
  become the serializer's opinion. Nothing fails and tests stay green, so it rides onward. Edit
  JSON as anchored text; if you must round-trip, pin every lossy default and read the resulting
  diff before committing. (Portable — a promote candidate for `repo-text-sweeps`, where a
  `\uXXXX`-in-tracked-JSON check would carry it.)
- **Test git fixtures must commit with signing off.** `engine-tests/helpers.mjs`'s `makeRepo`
  overrides identity but not signing, so all 31 call sites route fixture commits through the
  signing service; when it degrades, each commit blocks on it and the suite leaks descriptors
  (~800 per full run against a 4096 cap) until `git commit` and `git push` fail process-wide.
  Commit with `git -c commit.gpgsign=false commit --no-gpg-sign`: signing a tmpdir throwaway
  buys nothing. (Portable — a promote candidate for `writing-tests`.)
- **A canon session with a consumer repo also in its sources will reach for the *consumer's*
  merge skill — merge by the skill of the repo you are merging into.** Canon work is routinely
  dual-repo (the canon plus the fleet member being piloted), and both repos ship a merge skill
  under different names — the canon's `packs/git-github/skills/merge-to-main/` and, say, GCEC's
  local `merge-and-ci`. The consumer's skill wins the match on name/description and is followed
  to the letter, so the canon-only steps in *its* recipe are silently skipped — repeatedly, the
  **post-merge conversation capture** (`node packs/grow_with_claudinite/capture-log.mjs --issue
  <n>`, the "After the merge" section of `merge-to-main`). So: before merging in a dual-repo
  session, resolve the merge skill **by target repo**, not by which skill matched first — and
  treat capture as part of the merge, not as an optional epilogue.
- **Fail-soft SessionStart steps hide their own breakage fleet-wide — test the emitted
  output, not the exit code.** Every `engine/pack_loader/` SessionStart step
  (`inject-pack-prose.mjs`, `mount-skills.mjs`, `env-requirements.mjs`) wraps its body in
  `try { ... } catch {}` so a broken loader never blocks a session. That fail-soft is deliberate,
  but it means a runtime fault — a wrong dynamic-import target, a renamed module — exits 0 and
  simply emits nothing: no error, no signal. And because the engine is vendored verbatim into
  every member, one canon regression silently disables that step across the whole fleet at once.
  So a step like this must be guarded by a regression test that runs the real script against a
  real corpus and asserts the **positive** effect — prose IS emitted — never merely that
  `status === 0` (which fail-soft makes meaningless); see
  `engine-tests/pack_loader/inject-pack-prose.test.mjs`.
- **The nightly self-refresh cannot repair the vendor-set computation — pin operational
  files against the REAL canon tree.** Baselining's converge re-runs
  `vendoring/compute-vendor-set.mjs` from canon HEAD, so a bug *in that computation* is
  the one class of canon regression that is not self-healing: every refresh faithfully
  reproduces it, and recovery is an out-of-band vendor refresh applied to each member by
  hand. So when the vendor set excludes by *pattern*, an operational file that matches
  needs a by-path whitelist (`VENDORED_ENGINE_DOCS`) **and** a regression test asserting
  against the real canon tree, not only a synthetic fixture: a fixture keeps proving the
  whitelist mechanism works while the live path silently drops out from under it (see the
  paired tests in `vendoring/compute-vendor-set.test.mjs`).
- **You cannot force a due slot by running the scheduler workflow by hand.** Dueness is
  stateless — a slot is due iff its time falls in `(last successful run, now]` — so a
  `workflow_dispatch` run outside the slot's window succeeds, prints `- no tasks due`, and
  does nothing. It looks like a healthy run. To exercise a task Action-side, invoke its
  worker directly, or move the slot hour in `taskScheduler` and wait for the cron.
- **A scheduled task is gated twice — prove a change through `planRun`, never through its own
  precondition.** `planRun` computes the due list *before* any precondition runs, so a task whose
  most-recent slot has already been run is never evaluated and never reads its signals at all. #513's
  forced-run override landed with every test driving the precondition (or the signal collector) directly
  and was inert on exactly the run it existed for — the mid-day manual trigger — because the due-list
  gate it never touched had already dropped the task (`evaluations: []`; fixed in #516). A test that
  starts *inside* the gate proves only "works once evaluated" and says nothing about whether the task
  ever gets there. Drive the real `planRun` from a deliberately **non-due** slot: that is the only shape
  that catches it.
- **Every due task in a run shares ONE checkout — an agentless worker must not touch it.** The
  scheduler runs the whole due list in a single working tree, so a worker that checks out a branch or
  leaves an index behind hands the next task a tree it did not expect, and a run that dies leaves the
  mess for whatever follows. A task whose output is a regenerated file lands it through
  `engine/scheduler/deliver-generated.mjs` — git plumbing against the fetched base tip, with HEAD, the
  index and the working tree untouched — and reads its prior state from that base rather than local
  HEAD, so stacked runs stay idempotent. (`basics/baselining`'s own deliver is the deliberate
  exception: it commits a whole working tree under the member's delivery preference.)
- **A code-search hit is evidence; a code-search miss is not — survey by reading each file.**
- **Derive the test file list from the tree — every hand-written glob here under-runs the suite.**
  There is no `package.json` and no test script, so each session invents its own incantation and
  silently verifies less than it thinks. Measured in this checkout: `node --test <dir>` does not
  recurse — it resolves the path as a module and dies with `Cannot find module`; bash `**` is not
  recursive without `globstar`, so `engine-tests/**/*.test.mjs packs-tests/**/*.test.mjs` reaches
  **37 of 65** tracked test files. Four consecutive sessions (2026-07-26, #459/#452/#435/#468) each
  wrote a different command and reported 587, 690, 621 and 697 tests — three of them pushed after
  running a strict subset. Neither published list is authoritative either: `ci.yml`'s `tests=(…)`
  array omits `vendoring/*.test.mjs`, and `engine/checks/README.md`'s "as CI runs it" one-liner
  names `engine/test/`, `skills/` and `mount/`, none of which exist. So enumerate from git and let
  the count speak: `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')`. (The drift-guard, once the array is
  clean: assert every tracked `*.test.mjs` is matched by `ci.yml`'s globs.)
- **A branch that waited overnight has lost its base *and* possibly its premise — re-verify the
  problem still exists on current `main`, unasked.** This repo merges its own scheduled-task PRs
  without a human, on top of multi-phase migrations that retire whole directories: measured on
  PR #465, `main` moved **14 commits in 13.7 hours** and one of them (#473, "retire `run_daily/`")
  *deleted the file the PR's diagnosis rested on* and had already landed most of its content. The
  branch rebased cleanly and the tests stayed green — the change was simply no longer the change to
  make, and the correct move was `git checkout -B <branch> origin/main` and re-applying only the
  surviving slice (9 files → 2). So syncing the base is not the check; the check is a **content**
  one: after `git fetch`, read what the new commits did to the surface you are changing and state
  whether the problem is still there, what the goal was, and what survives. Do this whenever you
  return to a paused branch, before presenting it — the owner should never have to ask "is this
  change still needed" (asked three times on #465 before it was volunteered).
- **`subscribe_pr_activity` blocks for minutes — subscribe once, and never as a way to "wait for
  CI".** It reads like a cheap registration, so a session calls it, gets no answer, and calls it
  again on the same PR. Measured in the #520 session (`2026-07-28T2208Z`): two consecutive calls on
  PR #524 cost **237s + 220s**, and a `send_later` check-in a further **101s** — **558s of that
  session's 841s of total tool wall-clock (66%)**, all pure idle, in a session whose actual work was
  153 tool calls. One subscription per PR is all there is to gain; a second adds nothing but the
  wait. When what you actually want is "is it green yet", read the check status directly and merge
  on the already-green result — don't buy the same notification twice.
- **The home has no `.claudinite/shared/` mount — machinery paths must accept both roots.** A
  consumer runs the vendored engine under `.claudinite/shared/engine/…` with packs under
  `.claudinite/(shared|local)/packs/…`; the home *is* the corpus and runs the same code from the
  repo root. So a path, regex, or workflow command written to the consumer mount shape works
  fleet-wide and fails on exactly this repo — the last place anyone exercises it, so the break
  surfaces late. Write the two-root form up front: make the `.claudinite/(shared|local)/` prefix
  optional in a pattern, and in a command probe for `.claudinite/shared/` first, falling back to
  the repo root.

# Claudinite — where content goes (pack routing)

Each pack states what it owns and what it does not. When a rule, doc, skill or check could live in more than one, this table decides it — and "no pack fits" means a new pack or the project's own `local_packs/`, never the baseline by default.

| Pack | Belongs | Does not belong |
|---|---|---|
| `android` | gradle/AGP builds, AndroidManifest, permissions, signing configs, product flavors and emulator workflows for an Android app module | store submission and release cadence — play-store-release; Flutter-side widget or Dart code — flutter |
| `app-store-release` | shipping to the Apple App Store: App Store Connect, provisioning, App Attest, TestFlight, review guidelines, release cadence | iOS coding, Info.plist and Xcode project practices — that is ios; backend environment split — firebase-release |
| `aws-sam` | serverless AWS stacks: SAM template shape, Lambda handler paths, esbuild bundling, API Gateway and CloudFront gotchas | backend Google ID token validation — google-identity; generic Node packaging habits — node |
| `barriers` | directed folder-access graph rules — which directories may never reference which, plus the exceptions each rule allows | where a file should live or naming conventions — that is basics file-placement, not an access barrier |
| `basics` | cross-project working discipline, issue-branch-PR lifecycle, repo hygiene, doc/reference integrity and the baseline engineering, testing and debugging skills | technology-specific content — its own tech pack; GitHub Actions workflow or platform behaviour — github-actions; git procedure — git-github |

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

4. **Verify the outcome in code, then converge — then stop.** The declared `expected_outcome`
   is a **ceiling, not a target**: it is the most a task may do, and **"no change" is always
   legal** — a run that found nothing worth changing is a success, never a reason to
   manufacture work. Determine what the run did to pull requests and check it against that
   ceiling with `verify-outcome.mjs` — a `none` task that opened a PR, or an `open-pr` task
   that merged one, **fails the run**. Then:
   - Success within ceiling → comment the result and **close** the issue.
   - Failure (task failed, or ceiling violated) → comment naming what failed, remove
     `agent-running`, add `needs-human`. Do not close.

   Your issue is converged, so **your session's work is done**. Do not go looking for more.

5. **Capture this session before you end it.** Last step, after the issue is converged, and
   run it whichever way step 4 went — a failed run is the one most worth having a record of:

   ```bash
   CLAUDINITE_SESSION_ISSUE=<issue> node <engine>/hooks/session-end-command.mjs
   ```

   That runner invokes whatever session-end steps this repo's declared packs contribute; it
   knows nothing about what any of them do, and a repo that contributes none does nothing.
   Nobody is sitting in front of this session, so it ends by having its container reclaimed —
   which is precisely the ending that fires no `SessionEnd` hook. Left to the hook, every
   unattended run would leave no record of itself anywhere: not of the skills it loaded, not
   of the checks that caught something, not of how the work actually went. Run it here and it
   does.

   It cannot fail your dispatch — the issue is already converged and this changes nothing on
   GitHub. If it reports an error, **say so plainly in your final message** and end anyway.

**Two things are never yours to rescue:** a stale `agent-running` claim left by a session that
died mid-run, and a dispatch whose label event never landed. The scheduler converges both in
code on its hourly run (`dispatch.mjs` `staleClaimedDispatchIssues` and `rearmDispatchIssues`).
Leave them alone — recovery runs once, in one place, and it is not here.

# tidy-issues worker

The **acting** third of the repo tidy-up: triage the issues in scope, then record what you did. You run
under the executor, dispatched by a `ready-for-agent` issue; its **Context section is binding scope** — it
lists the issues to triage. Work only those; don't enumerate the repo yourself. GitHub access is
**MCP-only** (`mcp__github__*`).

The task's declared outcome ceiling is **`none`**: this task writes **issues only** (its triage actions and
its own tracker). It never opens, closes, merges, or comments on a PR, never touches a branch, and never
pushes — those dimensions belong to `tidy-prs` and `tidy-branches`, which are assess-only.

## 1. Triage each issue

For each issue in the Context list, run the [single-issue-triage](../../skills/single-issue-triage/SKILL.md)
skill. The skill owns the action ladder and the safeguards: "implemented in `main`" means the issue's actual
ask is true of `main`'s content **now** — verified there and cited, never inferred — and when the check is
inconclusive it **comments, doesn't close**. Collect what each triage did.

## 2. Reconcile this task's tracker

One standing tracker issue per repo, titled exactly `Claudinite tracker: Tidy Issues` — found by that
**exact title, never a fuzzy match**; create it **already closed** if absent (never a fresh issue per run,
never a bare number that can dangle). Each dimension keeps its **own** tracker, so three tasks never race
to rewrite one body.

Touch it two ways each run:

- **Rewrite the issue body** to today's **dated** snapshot: the actions taken this run and anything left
  for a human. The body is the live picture — it replaces yesterday's, it doesn't accumulate.
- **Add a dated comment** with today's status, so the body's snapshots leave a per-run trail.

Keep both short. **Never open, close, or reopen the tracker** — its state carries no meaning (the body is
the live picture; the state is just however it was created).

## 3. Retire the legacy tracker (transitional, one line of work)

Repos tidied before the split carry a single combined tracker titled exactly `Claudinite tracker: Repo
Tidy`. If it exists and its body doesn't already say so, rewrite the body to one line pointing at the three
per-dimension trackers (`Tidy Issues`, `Tidy PRs`, `Tidy Branches`) and stop there — nothing else to do on
it, and never open, close, or reopen it. Already pointing at them ⇒ skip. Absent ⇒ skip; never create it.

`model: sonnet` — the implemented-in-`main` call is judgment; the reconcile is mechanical aggregation.

# Single-issue triage

Triage **one** open issue and take the **first** applicable action. This **acts** — but every action
defaults to the reversible option when the check is inconclusive.

- **Already implemented in `main`** → **close** (`completed`) + a one-line comment citing where it
  landed.
- **Conflicts with a current guideline** → label `needs-decision` + a comment naming the conflict.
- **Blocked by another issue** → label `blocked` + a comment `blocked by #N`.
- **Small and quick to do** → label `quick-win` + a comment scoping it.
- **Else** → leave it.

**"Implemented in `main`" means the issue's actual ask is true of `main`'s content _now_** — confirm
it there and cite it. **Never** infer it from a linked PR merging or the issue merely looking done. If
you can't point to it, **comment, don't close.** Create a label if it's missing. Return `{ action,
note }` (action one of closed/needs-decision/blocked/quick-win/left).

{"number":568,"title":"Personal preferences belong to the fleet, not the canon — declare the home, and have the enforcer name it","body":"Owner request (2026-07-29). `Comment class: feature`.

> Personal preferences are the concern of a specific fleet's users. The preferences should live in the Sheepdog repo, and each consuming repo should have a `.claudinite` setting for preferences location. I understand that automatically populating this setting now is a problem because Sheepdog is not a special entity, but in the future bootstrapping won't be from Claudinite core, but from a per-fleet Shepherd repo (which will tell the consumers to use it for preferences). For now — please move the preferences, and set the setting in all projects. Have the Sheepdog pack set this setting in the repos.

## The problem

`preferences/.md` lived in the canon, and the session-start step fell back to a hardcoded `raw.githubusercontent.com/[REDACTED:env:CCR_TRIGGER_REPO]/main/preferences` URL. The canon is mounted by **every** fleet that adopts Claudinite, which makes it both the wrong host for one owner's personal preferences and the wrong authority on where they live.

## The requirement

1. Preferences move out of the canon into the fleet's own repo (`missingbulb/Sheepdog`).
2. A consuming repo declares **where** its users' preferences live, as a setting in its own `.claudinite-checks.json`; the session-start step resolves that pointer instead of a constant.
3. Nothing in canon/bootstrap populates the pointer — a bootstrap run does not know which fleet it is bootstrapping into. The **sheepdog pack** (the per-fleet enforcer, the "Shepherd repo" of the request) writes it into the fleet's repos, so the fleet is what tells its members.

## Resolution

- missingbulb/Sheepdog#35 — the repo becomes the home (`preferences/`, one `.md` per person).
- #567 — the `preferences` setting + its one resolver, the session-start step that reads it, the canon's own `preferences/` removed, and the sheepdog pack's fourth sweep (`fleet-preferences`) that writes the pointer into every member — gated on each member's own vendored engine accepting the key, so the rollout needs no coordination.","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/[REDACTED:env:CCR_TRIGGER_REPO]/issues/568","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-07-29T22:29:02Z","updated_at":"2026-07-29T22:29:02Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false}

{"number":565,"title":"baselining's maintenance PR gets no CI — auto-merge arms against a green that never comes","body":"The same class of bug as #432, in the task that runs in **every consuming repo** rather than canon-only — found on baselining's first-ever real delivery (GoogleCalendarEventCreator, 2026-07-29).

## Observed

GCEC's scheduler run at 03:46 UTC ran the deterministic converge, pushed `claudinite/maintenance-2026-07-29-6049na`, opened PR GoogleCalendarEventCreator#781, and armed auto-merge. Twelve hours later the PR head had **zero check runs and zero statuses** (`mergeable_state: unstable`), while `main` moved three commits past its base. The agent stage (dispatch issue GoogleCalendarEventCreator#782) correctly no-op'd — nothing in the design ever re-visits the PR. It was unstuck only by a human session re-pushing the same branch under a user token, at which point CI started within a minute and auto-merge fired on green.

## Why

`worker.mjs` `deliver()` pushes the branch and opens the PR over the Action's `GITHUB_TOKEN`. GitHub suppresses workflow runs for events authored by that token, so no `pull_request` (or `push`) run ever starts — the exact rule the canon documents in git-github-advanced, and the one #432 hit in `migrations-retire`. The #432 fix (open the PR over `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN`) was applied to that canon-only task; baselining, which runs fleet-wide, still walks into it. Since `deliver()` reuses the family PR by prefix and force-pushes each cycle, the PR stalls permanently, night over night.

## Fix

Not the PAT route — most members will never configure `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN`, and baselining must work everywhere out of the box. Use the documented exception instead: `workflow_dispatch` events created with `GITHUB_TOKEN` **do** start runs (this is empirically proven fleet-side — GCEC's scheduler dispatches `chrome-extension-release.yml` with the same token nightly, `triggering_actor: github-actions[bot]`, and a dispatched run's check runs attach to the branch-head SHA, which is what the PR's merge gate reads).

So `deliver()`, after the force-push: read the repo's workflow files on the maintenance branch, pick those that would have run on `pull_request` **and** carry `workflow_dispatch`, and POST a dispatch for each with `ref: `. Warn (don't fail) when a `pull_request` workflow lacks the `workflow_dispatch` trigger, naming the file — that's the owner's one-line fix. The scheduler workflow already grants `actions: write`.

Canon's own `ci.yml` is `pull_request`-only, so it also gets `workflow_dispatch:` added — which retroactively makes option 2 of #432 available too.

{"number":564,"title":"Pack manifests as JSON: pack.json + pack.schema.json, code split into sibling files","body":"Owner comment (process-change): "Why are packs declared using mjs? Is it just the `detect` part? It seems they can all be just JSON declarations, and if we have some code that detects, we can put that in a different file. And once it's just JSON — can't you declare the schema in a nicer way than `engine/pack_loader/pack-schema.mjs`? You can still have validations (a simple unit test) for making sure all the skills/rules are declared and there's no drift, but at least the files will be sane."

Measured across the 29 manifests (27 canon + the home's 2 local packs): **988 lines, 56 of them `import` statements, 350 of them comments.** Almost nothing in a `pack.mjs` needs to be code.

## What is actually code today

| Field | Packs | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `detect` | 13 (14 declare `null`) | ~10 are one-liners over `ctx.tracked` — `includes`, `endsWith`, a path regex, or the shared `hasMarkerNearRoot` helper — all expressible as data. **3 need real logic**: `chrome-extension` (locates the extension manifest), `chrome-extension-release` (recognizes a release orchestrator workflow), `leaflet` (scans file *content*). |
| `worldRules` / `workRules` | all | Code only as *imports*. In JSON these become filenames the loader imports. |
| `env` | 2 | Genuinely code — `setup`/`probe` are functions of the pack's config returning shell. |
| `contributes` / `contributedRules` | 3 / 1 | `contributes` is a map of pack id → rule modules, so filenames. `contributedRules` (barriers only) is a real seam. |
| everything else | — | Pure data: `id`, `badge`, `marker`, `prose`, `seededByDefault`, `requires`, `ruleRoutingGuidance`, `skills`, `questions`. |

## Shape wanted

- `packs//pack.json` for all 29, with `$schema` pointing at a `pack.schema.json`.
- Optional sibling code files, named from the JSON, only where needed: `detect.mjs` (3 packs), `env.mjs` (2), `contributed-rules.mjs` (1).
- Rules referenced **by filename**, which buys a drift guard the current shape cannot have: every rule `.mjs` in the pack directory must appear in exactly one of the two scope lists. Today an undeclared rule module is simply invisible.

## Why it is worth more than tidiness

**The loader stops executing arbitrary code at load.** Today a consumer's local `pack.mjs` is `import()`ed during SessionStart in every session and on every check run — which is precisely why `pack-registry.mjs` carries per-pack import isolation. With JSON, the ~26 packs that need no code execute none.

**A real schema.** `pack.schema.json` gives editor autocomplete and validation that `PACK_FIELDS` never will.

## What it costs

1. **The 350 comment lines have nowhere to go** — and they are real rationale, not noise: why `basics` requires `barriers` and contributes the isolation barrier as manifest data, why `canon-curation`'s declaration cardinality is what makes its tasks central-once. The natural home is the pack README, which is now exactly the "rationale the manifest cannot carry" file after #559 — this brings two or three of the deleted ones back.
2. **`pack.mjs` is a consumer-held shape**, not only ours — every member repo has local packs. Needs both-shapes tolerance plus a baseline migration to retire the old one, per `consumer-safe-changes.md`.

## Scope note on validation

A consumer's local pack must be validated at *their* Stop hook, not this repo's CI, so loader-side validation stays. JSON Schema replaces the **field-shape** half of `pack-schema.mjs`; the **cross-file drift guards** (skills ↔ directory, rules ↔ files) remain loader checks with unit tests over them. Net effect: that module shrinks substantially rather than disappearing.

{"number":409,"title":"Tracking-issue freshness: keep the plan issue in sync after every merge","body":"Implementation tracker for the tracking-issue freshness check. This issue is itself an instance of the pattern it tracks — it carries the live checklist; the committed doc carries the rationale.

**Read first (on `main`):**
- Design + plan — [`docs/tracking-issue-freshness/DESIGN.md`](https://github.com/[REDACTED:env:CCR_TRIGGER_REPO]/blob/main/docs/tracking-issue-freshness/DESIGN.md)

**The problem:** a major task has two artifacts — a source-controlled design/migration plan and a GitHub tracking issue with a `- [ ]`/`- [x]` checklist (the "read status and pick up the work" point). When a phase lands, the committed plan's status is updated in the same PR (the diff forces review), but the issue checklist is a separate surface no diff touches, so it silently drifts. Already live: `per-project-scheduling/MIGRATION.md` says Phase 1 is "same day, no soak" while #394's Phase 1 item still says "Soak ~1 week."

**The design, in two surfaces:**
1. **In-session (timely):** a transcript-only post-merge check-the-work rule — `in-session-github-access` (blocking) means in-session code has no GitHub REST credential, so the rule reads the merge, the tracker discovery, and the post-merge checklist edit from the session transcript's MCP tool calls. Enablers: `work.mergedThisSession()` and a Stop-hook post-merge trigger (the merge recipe leaves a clean tree, which would otherwise fast-exit).
2. **Nightly (convergent):** plans state, per phase, *how completion is decided* — a checklist item may carry `` naming a dependency-free Node script whose **exit 0 means the phase is done** ("if this code passes, phase 3 is done"); no marker ⇒ the phase's prose **Verify** block in the plan doc is the criteria. The `plan-status-update` task (daily, gated on an open `plan-tracking` issue) re-derives every tracker's checklist from these verifiers — flipping what sessions missed, flagging (never auto-un-flipping) a checked item whose code verifier now fails.

**Invariant:** any open `plan-tracking` issue must carry a todo checklist and have a box **flipped** in the same session as each merge that advances it (after the merge, not before — an item isn't done until it's on `main`). The issue *count* is not enforced.

**Phases (detail in the design doc):**
- [ ] **Convention + seed** — define the `plan-tracking` label and its meaning in the `grow_with_claudinite` / merge docs; apply it to existing in-flight tracker(s) (#394).
- [ ] **Primitive + trigger** — `work.mergedThisSession()` (transcript-derived accepted PRs) and the Stop hook's post-merge trigger, each with red-first tests.
- [ ] **Verifier (in-session)** — the `plan-tracking-freshness` rule in `grow_with_claudinite`; fires when a merge happened with no post-merge checklist flip, quiet otherwise.
- [ ] **Recipe wiring** — `merge-to-main` gains the "sync the `plan-tracking` issue after the merge" step (prose asks; the check guarantees).
- [ ] **Docs** — the convention in the pack README; design-doc status box; this issue points at the doc.
- [ ] **Per-phase verifiers (convention)** — `` code verifiers (exit 0 ⇒ done) with prose Verify blocks as fallback; recorded in the pack README and the nightly worker doc.
- [ ] **Nightly status update** — the `plan-status-update` task (daily/sonnet/none, gated on an open `plan-tracking` issue): re-verifies each tracker, flips passes, flags regressions in a comment.

{"number":498,"title":"scheduler-workflow-shape should validate the scopes a repo's tasks actually need, not a fixed two","body":"Surfaced by the `growth-extract` run on #484, and pulled out of that run's RULES.md entries during review: this reads as a proposed mechanism change rather than a rule a session can follow, so filing it here instead.

## The gap

`packs/basics/scheduler-workflow-shape.mjs` validates exactly two permissions on a repo's `claudinite-scheduler.yml`, both hard-coded:

```
if (!/^\s*contents:\s*write\b/m.test(text))       → flag
if (!/^\s*pull-requests:\s*write\b/m.test(text))  → flag
```

Those two cover baselining's `deliver()` (push a branch, open a PR, arm auto-merge). They cover nothing a *task's worker* needs. So a task whose worker calls a GitHub endpoint requiring some third scope passes the check with a stub that never granted it, and the failure lands at runtime in a member repo.

## How it actually bit (#478)

`store-release`'s worker POSTs a `workflow_dispatch`, which needs `actions: write`. The stub granted `actions: read`. Every fire 403'd, the worker exited 1, and the scheduler converged the task to `needs-human` — leaving three cut-over members with no working release path. Nothing caught it earlier because nothing was looking: the check validates a fixed pair, and the next task needing a fourth scope will land exactly the same way.

## Suggested direction

Make the required scope set *derived* rather than fixed. Roughly:

1. Let a task declare what its worker needs in its `task.mjs` — e.g. `required_scopes: ['actions:write']` — alongside the existing `agent_model` / `expected_outcome` fields, validated by `task-contract.mjs`.
2. Have `scheduler-workflow-shape` union the declared scopes across the repo's enabled tasks with the baselining floor (`contents:write`, `pull-requests:write`) and assert the workflow grants each one, naming the task that needs it in the failure message.
3. Have the stub generator emit the union, so a repo that adopts a task gets the grant with it rather than hand-editing `engine/scheduler/stubs/claudinite-scheduler.yml`.

That turns "read the scope off the endpoint and grant it yourself, and hope you remembered" into a declaration the check enforces. Worth weighing against the simpler option — keep the check fixed but widen the floor to include `actions: write` — which costs a broader default token but no new contract surface.

Not started; opening for a decision on which direction (or neither) before any implementation.

Refs #484, #478","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/[REDACTED:env:CCR_TRIGGER_REPO]/issues/498","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","labels":["needs-decision"],"comments":1,"reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-07-27T18:57:40Z","updated_at":"2026-07-28T07:33:37Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false}

{"number":422,"title":"Wire the canon's executor Routines (self + fleet) — last step of the scheduler cutover","body":"The canon's own scheduler landed in #421 (Refs #394). The scheduler evaluates the canon's tasks hourly; agentless ones run inline (`baselining` self-skips, `migrations-retire` archives), and agentful ones file `[claudinite-task]` issues for an **executor Routine** to run. Executor Routines are a Claude Code Routine + settings change, not code — the one remaining manual step.

Per the **self/fleet split** (#421), there are **two** executors, distinguished by trigger label, so the fleet-wide session grant stays off the self executor:

### 1. Self executor — every repo (incl. the canon)
```
Name:            Claudinite executor
Trigger:         GitHub issue-label event — `ready-for-agent` applied
Session model:   sonnet
Launcher prompt: Execute the Claudinite executor: engine/scheduler/executor.md
Sources:         [REDACTED:env:CCR_TRIGGER_REPO]  (this repo alone — self tasks touch only their own repo)
```
Runs: `growth-extract`, `growth-dedup`, `conversation-extract`, `growth-discover-packs`, `prose-to-checks-sweep`, `repo-tidy`. **A Routine (poke-only base) was created — `Claudinite executor` (`trig_01S7nEHSd4eQ2832jLDjdSEz`).** Finish it in settings: attach the **GitHub connector** (required — the created Routine stored none, so it'd run without `mcp__github__*`), set the trigger to the `ready-for-agent` label, model `sonnet`, sources = Claudinite alone.

### 2. Fleet executor — only repos with a fleet task (today: the canon)
```
Name:            Claudinite executor (fleet)
Trigger:         GitHub issue-label event — `ready-for-agent-fleet` applied
Session model:   sonnet
Launcher prompt: Execute the Claudinite executor: engine/scheduler/executor.md
Sources:         the owner's repos  (a fleet task reads across them — e.g. growth-promote reads every member's local packs)
```
Runs: `growth-promote` only. Same settings to finish (GitHub connector, label filter `ready-for-agent-fleet`, model `sonnet`, broader sources).

### Notes
- **Canon path:** both prompts use `engine/scheduler/executor.md` (repo root) — the canon runs its own engine, no vendored mount. (A consumer's self executor would use `.claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/executor.md`; `executor.md` resolves this itself.)
- **Labels:** the scheduler creates `ready-for-agent`, `ready-for-agent-fleet`, `agent-running`, `needs-human`, `workflow-failure` on its first dispatch (create-if-missing). To wire a Routine's label filter *before* that first run, create the label(s) in the GitHub UI first: `ready-for-agent` `#0e8a16`, `ready-for-agent-fleet` `#1d76db`.
- `growth-promote` also needs `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN` as a repo Actions secret (the workflow passes it through). Absent, `growth-promote` skips cleanly and the self tasks still run.

Close this once both Routines are wired.","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/[REDACTED:env:CCR_TRIGGER_REPO]/issues/422","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-07-24T06:52:02Z","updated_at":"2026-07-26T09:58:53Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false}

{"number":379,"title":"Vendored-mount flip isn't fleet-ready: MCP push_files can't land the canon vendor in one commit, fixed-branch re-dispatch races, and the .claude write prompt suspends unattended runs (GCEC pilot)","body":"The 2026-07-21 fleet daily maintenance run attempted the `vendored-mount-flip` on its sole pilot member (`flip.repos: ['missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator']`). It failed on **structural** grounds, not a one-off fluke. GCEC's `main` was never touched (still pre-flip, legacy `.claudinite/mount`, no stamp) so nothing is broken — but the flip mechanism is not ready to run unattended or to widen.

## What happened
The flip must vendor the entire canon snapshot — `.claudinite/shared/**`, ~240 KB across hundreds of files — into the member. The migration/worker contract says land **one** content commit (then a separate `delete_file` for the legacy hook). In practice:

1. **`push_files` can't carry the vendor tree in one commit (size limit).** The worker fell back to committing in batches — `Claudinite: vendor the canon snapshot (batch 1/11)`, `2/11`, `3/11`, … — directly contradicting the "one content commit" contract. Any batching here must be deterministic, idempotent, and resumable; today it isn't specified.

2. **The fixed `claudinite/maintenance` branch races under re-dispatch.** The first attempt suspended on the `.claude/settings.json` permission prompt (see #3); a second worker was dispatched while the first was still live, and **both wrote the same fixed branch with different batch plans** — the log interleaves `batch 3/11`, then `batch 2/10`, then `batch 4/11` (two denominators = two writers). A fixed, shared branch name has no single-writer guarantee; re-dispatch duplicates/races. Needs a per-attempt branch or a real single-writer/idempotent-convergence guard.

3. **The `.claude/settings.json` write suspends an unattended run indefinitely.** Repointing the SessionStart/Stop/PreToolUse hooks triggers an interactive permission prompt. Unanswered, it left the worker idle for ~hours (surfaced as a bogus multi-hour "runtime"). The flip cannot be an unattended nightly operation while that prompt exists — it must be gated to an attended path or a pre-authorized allow-rule.

4. **A batched/raced landing leaves an ambiguous half-flipped branch.** The abandoned branch had `.claudinite/shared/` only partially vendored, the legacy `.claudinite/mount` **not** deleted, no `claudinite` stamp, and no PR. The preconditions (pre-flip / half-flipped / flipped) assume a near-atomic landing and don't cover "partial vendor from a batched/raced push."

5. **Cleanup gap: the fleet session can't delete the junk branch.** After a failed flip, the abandoned `claudinite/maintenance` branch can't be removed from the maintenance session — the git proxy `403`s a branch-delete push and the GitHub MCP exposes no delete-branch / delete-ref tool (only `create_branch`). So even cleanup after a failed flip needs a manual step.

## Recommendation
- **Do not widen `flip.repos`** beyond the pilot, and treat the flip as **not nightly-ready**.
- Before retrying: (a) an MCP-batch-aware *or* alternative landing that survives `push_files` limits, deterministic + resumable; (b) single-writer / per-attempt-branch handling so re-dispatch can't race; (c) move the `.claude/settings.json` write behind an attended or pre-authorized gate; (d) precondition handling for a partially-vendored branch; (e) a way for the session to delete an abandoned flip branch (or avoid creating one until the landing is atomic).

## Housekeeping
- GCEC `main` is safe (pre-flip, coherent). No cleanup needed there.
- The abandoned `missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator` branch `claudinite/maintenance` (5 orphan "vendor the canon snapshot" commits, no PR) needs **manual deletion** — the session couldn't remove it (see #5).

Relates to #315 (vendored-mount design), #335 (flip strands docs / phase-3 sweep). Source: the `2026-07-18-vendored-mount-flip` note.

_Filed by the fleet daily maintenance run of 2026-07-21 (owner-directed)._","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/[REDACTED:env:CCR_TRIGGER_REPO]/issues/379","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-07-21T09:44:55Z","updated_at":"2026-07-21T09:44:55Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false}

{"number":381,"title":"Restructure the tree so the engine and content copy as clean folders (engine/, engine-tests/, packs-tests/, skills-tests/)","body":"Restructure the repo so each copyable unit is one clean folder:

- **`engine/`** — the whole engine in one folder, copyable without tests: `engine/checks/` (runner, lib, Stop hook, PreToolUse guard), `engine/mount/` (vendor writer, session-start orchestrator, sync/env-setup scripts), and the pack/skill machinery moved off the content roots into `engine/packs/` (registry, load-active-prose, env, interview) and `engine/skills/` (registry, mount-skills).
- **`engine-tests/`** — mirrors the engine's subfolders (`checks/`, `mount/`, `packs/`, `skills/`), absorbing the former `checks/test/` and the in-tree `*.test.mjs`.
- **`packs-tests//`** — each pack's tests **and its maintainer-notes README**, so `packs//` holds only payload (prose, checks, stubs) and copies clean.

{"number":331,"title":"Notes v2 retention window silently orphans out-of-scope members — add a stamp-staleness alarm + census/scope reconciliation","body":"From a design review of `mount/DESIGN.md` (#315).

**Problem.** Retirement by retention window (~5 weeks, DESIGN.md §9) inverts the failure direction of the old telemetry-gated design. The old design failed *open* — an invisible repo held retirement hostage (annoying, safe). Notes v2 fails toward **orphaning**: notes are deleted on calendar time, and the doc's claim that a lagging repo "has been failing loudly in the nightly log (**or was off the access list**)" is untrue for exactly the parenthetical case — the nightly logs failures only for repos the session was *handed*; a member that drops out of the granted MCP scope logs nothing anywhere, silently stops updating, and sails past its catch-up window into the re-adoption path without anyone noticing.

**Fix.**
- **Stamp-staleness alarm** — now structurally cheap: the stamp lives in the tracked `.claudinite-checks.json`, the single probe every member carries whatever its mount shape (phase 1's own discovery reduction). "Stamp older than N days" fires well *inside* the retention window (e.g. alarm at 2 weeks vs. a 5-week window), to the fleet routine's failure log.
- **Reconcile the census's account-wide covered set against the session's granted scope** — a census-covered member absent from the grant is exactly the silent case; surface it loudly.
- Optionally key retention off the **oldest live stamp observed** rather than the calendar alone, so the window can't out-run a visible laggard.","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/[REDACTED:env:CCR_TRIGGER_REPO]/issues/331","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-07-18T19:49:34Z","updated_at":"2026-07-18T19:49:34Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false}

{"number":276,"title":"Move chrome-extension-release plumbing out of core `.github/` into the pack (vendored into consumers)","body":"Resolves the **RELEASE** item of #270: the reusable release workflows (`.github/workflows/chrome-extension-*.yml` + `deploy-privacy-page.yml`) and the three composite actions (`read-release-config`, `bump-extension-patch`, `report-failure`) live in Claudinite's core tree but exist solely for the `chrome-extension-release` pack. They must move behind the pack that owns them, leaving Claudinite with no release-specific GitHub Actions.

## Decision (agreed with owner)

- **Hosting model: vendor into each consumer.** GitHub only resolves reusable workflows/composite actions from a repo's own `.github/`, never from a `packs/…` subdir, so "into the pack" means the pack holds the templates and each consumer hosts a *managed* copy in its own `.github/`. Consumers become self-contained; baselining (not the consumer) owns keeping the copies correct. This reverses the original "thin consumer" design — deliberately.
- **Phase-2 deletion: automatic, telemetry-gated.** Once the fleet census confirms every consumer has vendored, the census deletes Claudinite's release plumbing automatically as part of migration retirement — no follow-up PR.
- **Secrets: nothing to migrate.** The four `CHROME_*` secrets already live in each consumer repo (they travel via `secrets: inherit` from the consumer's own workflow); Claudinite holds none.

## Plan

1. **Pack = source of truth.** Move the 4 workflows + 3 composite actions into `packs/chrome-extension-release/` as vendored templates; rewrite cross-repo `uses: [REDACTED:env:CCR_TRIGGER_REPO]/.github/…@main` → local `uses: ./.github/…`; rename to avoid the in-repo filename collision (the orchestrator and the create-package reusable are both `chrome-extension-release.yml` today).
2. **Migration is the fix vehicle.** A new baseline migration carries: (a) a **materialize** op — baselining writes the vendored set into each consumer's `.github/` and drops the old thin-stub `@main` refs; (b) a **legacyPresent** probe ("still references `[REDACTED:env:CCR_TRIGGER_REPO]/.github/workflows/chrome-extension-*`") for fleet telemetry; (c) a **retire-deletes-from-home** list — Claudinite's own release files. Extend the migration mechanism (today rename-only) with the materialize op, and teach the census to delete the home-repo files on retirement.
3. **Tolerant checks during transition.** The `cer/*` checks accept both the old thin-stub shape and the new vendored shape until the migration retires, so no consumer's check suite goes red mid-flight.
4. **Docs.** Update `RELEASE.md`, `.github/workflows/README.md` (drop the frozen-`@main`-API section), and the pack fingerprint.

## Prerequisite for the automatic cut

The automatic phase-2 deletion needs `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN` granted **Contents-write on the home repo** — #239 notes this is not granted yet. Until it is, the census logs "grant FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN Contents write" and Claudinite's copies stay in place (harmless — consumers already run off their vendored copies by then).

{"number":270,"title":"Shrink the core⟂pack accept-map to {}: remaining core→pack/skill couplings","body":"Follow-up to #269 / #268. The core⟂pack independence guard (`checks/test/core-independence.test.mjs`) now blocks any *new* core→pack/skill coupling, but it ships green with the current couplings recorded in its **accept-map**. Shrinking that map to `{}` is the standing goal; this issue tracks the deferred entries ("the rest"). Each accept-map entry names its file and a reason — that's the living worklist; the items below group them.

### 1. SEEDING — the engine hardcodes default-seeded pack names
`checks/run.mjs` carries `const seeded = ['basics', 'grow_with_claudinite', 'tidy-repo'];`. The engine shouldn't know specific pack names. **Fix direction:** let a pack declare its own default-seed policy (e.g. `detect: null` + a `seededByDefault` flag) so bootstrap/`run.mjs` discover it structurally. Also touches `bootstrap.md`, which describes the same seeding by pack name.

### 2. RELEASE — chrome-extension-release infra hosted in core `.github/`
The reusable release workflows (`.github/workflows/chrome-extension-*.yml`) and the `read-release-config` action live in the core tree but exist solely for the `chrome-extension-release` pack. **Decide:** whether this plumbing should move to live behind the pack that owns it, or is legitimately shared canon CI.

### 3. DOC_CITES — engine/design docs naming packs/skills as examples (**the "skills — discuss later" set**)
`checks/DESIGN.md`, `extending.md`, `growth/*.md`, `README.md`, `consumer-safe-changes.md`, etc. cite specific packs/skills by name as illustrative examples (e.g. "per the `unattended-agents` skill", "e.g. the `tidy-repo` pack"). Not a runtime coupling — nothing breaks — but by the strict rule (not by name, not in comments) they still name content. **Decide the policy:** may an engine/design doc name a pack/skill as an example, or must it speak generically? This is the skills question deferred from #269.

### 4. SEED_MIGRATION — one-time seed migrations name their target pack (likely accept-forever)
`migrations/2026-07-12-tidy-repo-seed.mjs`, `migrations/2026-07-12-grow-with-claudinite-seed.mjs` necessarily name the single pack they seed, and self-retire once the fleet converges. Probably a permanent, reasoned accept rather than a fix — noted for completeness.

### Open design question — where the planner runs
The decoupled planner (`routines/fleet/plan.mjs`) currently runs **in the maintenance session** over the *accessible* fleet (matching "the planner should just go over all accessible repositories"). The alternative is a dedicated **core planner GitHub Action** with an account-spanning token. If the Action model is preferred, that's a contained follow-up (a workflow + token, independent of the sheepdog census).

---
Definition of done: the accept-map is `{}` (or only holds reasoned, permanent entries like SEED_MIGRATION), and the planner-host decision is recorded.

{"number":223,"title":"Conformance-backlog: check for chrome-extension:// in API Gateway v2 CORS AllowOrigins","body":"Filed by the growth **promote** run of 2026-07-11 (PR #222, tracker #99).

One aws-sam lesson promoted in #222 landed as **prose** but has a static signature in a SAM/CloudFormation template, so it's a candidate for the promotion ladder's **rung-3 conformance check** — deferred to prose because a confident detection + red/green fixture couldn't be authored unattended in that run.

**Rule (already prose in `packs/aws-sam/RULES.md`):** API Gateway HTTP API (v2) rejects a `chrome-extension://` origin in CORS `AllowOrigins` (`BadRequestException: Invalid format for origin`) — it accepts only `http(s)://…` or `*`.

**Possible check:** in the aws-sam pack, scan a SAM template's `AWS::Serverless::HttpApi` / `AWS::ApiGatewayV2::Api` `CorsConfiguration.AllowOrigins` (and `Cors`/`AllowOrigins` shorthands) for any entry whose scheme is not `http`/`https` and not `*` — the failure message being the prose above. Needs care around CloudFormation intrinsics (`!Ref`, `!Sub`, `Fn::If`) and a fixture proving it fires on a `chrome-extension://` origin and stays quiet on `['*']` / `https://…`.

Sweep later via the `prose-to-checks` pass; not a blocker for #222.","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/[REDACTED:env:CCR_TRIGGER_REPO]/issues/223","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","labels":["conformance-backlog"],"reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-07-11T00:35:58Z","updated_at":"2026-07-11T00:35:58Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false}

{"number":170,"title":"Revisit: Workflow tool's interactive opt-in blocks unattended routines (waiting on Anthropic)","body":"## The limitation

The multi-agent-orchestration **`Workflow`** tool requires an **interactive human opt-in on every run** ("Allow Claude to run a workflow?"). That prompt only disappears under bypass-permissions / headless modes a scheduler can't be relied on to be in. Because an unattended routine has no human to click **Allow**, any routine that fans out through the Workflow tool stalls on step one.

This also means the tool's nicest ergonomics are off-limits to us for unattended work: committing a Workflow script and having the nightly job just run it by name (`Workflow({name: ...})`) hits the **same** prompt — the gate is on *invoking* a workflow, not on authoring one. And the parallel-agent step can't be pushed into a plain committed script either, since spawning Claude subagents is a harness capability, not something arbitrary code can call.

## Our current workaround

We fan the fleet daily maintenance routine out with **plain subagent dispatch** (the Agent/Task tool) instead, which carries no opt-in gate, and the orchestrator honors the phase barriers itself. See #168 / #169 and `routines/auto-all-repos-maintenance.md` + `skills/unattended-agents/SKILL.md`.

This works and is the right default (no dependency on an out-of-repo permission-mode setting), but it costs us the Workflow tool's built-in phase/barrier machinery and the option to run committed, reviewed orchestration code.

## Why keep this open

This is a limitation of the platform, not our code — we're **waiting on the world to change**. If Anthropic later lets an unattended session pre-authorize the Workflow tool (a settings allowlist entry, an environment/routine permission mode that reliably suppresses just this prompt, or persisted per-workflow consent that survives a fresh cloud clone), we could reconsider using committed Workflow scripts for the fleet routine and get determinism + review back.

**Action:** periodically check with Anthropic / the Claude Code release notes whether the Workflow tool can be pre-authorized for unattended sessions. When it can, revisit the plain-dispatch decision in the routine spec.

[Resource from github at repo://[REDACTED:env:CCR_TRIGGER_REPO]/sha/92316951e0705d72c550d461fc73ecd3fead63bc/contents/.github/workflows/ci.yml] # The CANON repo's own CI — Claudinite's test suite + its own conformance sweep
# on every PR. Not consumer wiring (consumers ship no workflow, #385).
name: CI
on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  # Dispatchable so a GITHUB_TOKEN-authored PR (whose push/open GitHub never
  # turns into a pull_request run — the recursion guard) can still get this
  # suite started on its branch: baselining's deliver() and any bot flow like
  # migrations-retire's archive PR (#432, #565) dispatch it explicitly.
  workflow_dispatch:
defaults:
  run:
    shell: bash
jobs:
  test-and-conformance:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # Check out the PR's real head, not the synthetic refs/pull/N/merge commit
          # actions/checkout uses by default — otherwise HEAD is an ephemeral merge of
          # the branch into main, which the work-scoped squash-merge-history check would
          # (correctly, for that synthetic commit) flag. This makes CI evaluate exactly
          # what the local Stop hook does: the branch tip. Falls back to github.sha on push.
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
      - name: Unit tests
        # THE test roots — a closed set of FOLDERS, each swept to any depth. Depth is
        # deliberately not enumerated: the previous form spelled out one glob per level
        # (`packs-tests/*/skills/*/*.test.mjs` and so on), so a test at an unlisted depth
        # was silently never run — which is exactly how vendoring/'s two files sat outside
        # CI. `**` removes depth from the question; what remains is the root list, and
        # engine-tests/ci-test-roots.test.mjs fails the moment a tracked test lands
        # outside it. Adding a root is a deliberate CI edit; adding a test is not.
        #   engine-tests/            engine/ + the other top-level canon code (migrations/, …);
        #                            mirrors engine/'s inner structure, and stays canon-side
        #                            because engine/ ships to consumers exactly as-is (#385)
        #   packs-tests/             every canon pack's tests, mirroring packs/
        #   vendoring/               co-located with the vendor computer/writer they cover
        #   dev/tools/               maintainer-side tooling nothing at session time runs
        #   .claudinite/local/packs/ this repo's own local packs — tests live inside the tree
        # nullglob: a root with no tests drops out instead of reaching node as a literal pattern.
        run: |
          shopt -s globstar nullglob
          tests=(engine-tests/**/*.test.mjs packs-tests/**/*.test.mjs vendoring/**/*.test.mjs dev/tools/**/*.test.mjs .claudinite/local/packs/**/*.test.mjs)
          node --test "${tests[@]}"
      - name: Conformance sweep
        # The world sweep's home is the test/CI flow (not the Stop hook, which
        # carries only the work scope) — this canon repo models the pattern
        # bootstrap wires into consumers. World only: the work scope judges a
        # session's change and runs at that session's Stop hook, not here.
        run: node engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs
      - name: Promote write-surface gate
        # The growth promote stage (.claudinite/local/packs/canon-curation/tasks/growth-promote/task.md)
        # is the one change bounded to packs/ + skills/ — an ordinary engine PR legitimately edits
        # checks/ and engine/, so this cannot run on every PR. It keys on the promote branch prefix
        # (the task doc pins it) and fails the promote PR if a changed path strays.
        if: contains(github.head_ref, 'growth-promote')
        run: node .claudinite/local/packs/canon-curation/promote-scope.mjs
