[Resource from github at repo://[REDACTED:env:CCR_TRIGGER_REPO]/sha/92316951e0705d72c550d461fc73ecd3fead63bc/contents/vendoring/DESIGN.md] # The vendored mount — persist Claudinite in each consumer, update nightly (design)

> **Status: agreed direction (issue #315); phase 0 implemented, phase 1 in progress.** This doc is
> the decision record for replacing the session-start fetch with a tracked, nightly-updated
> vendor of the corpus. The live mount ([README.md](README.md)) keeps working unchanged until the
> transition phases land.

## The problem

Both mount methods re-fetch the corpus at every session start — Method B pulls the latest-`main`
tarball, Method A updates the submodule. That makes session start network-dependent and fragile:
the fetch halt-gate, the `codeload.github.com` allowlist requirement, the `.claudinite.new` swap,
and the tracked-copy preservation dance in the sync hook all exist only to manage fetch failure.
The freshness the fetch buys is not needed: the core rarely changes, packs change roughly
nightly, and nothing requires immediate propagation. So the per-session fetch pays a reliability
cost every session for a latency guarantee nothing uses.

## The model

**A consumer holds a vendored, tracked corpus at `.claudinite/shared/`** — ordinary committed
files at canon-relative paths, the same move issue #276 already made for the release workflows,
applied to the whole corpus. The **nightly maintenance is the only regular writer**.

1. **The `shared/` root is a submodule emulation.** The set materializes under
   `.claudinite/shared/` mirroring the canon layout exactly, so the planned future — mounting
   Claudinite as a **git submodule** at that same path, once sessions run where a cross-repo git
   credential exists — is a drop-in upgrade: the submodule lands a superset at the same root and
   **no wiring path changes**
   (`node .claudinite/shared/engine/hooks/stop-command.mjs`, …). This is also why nothing consumer-owned
   lives inside it: `.claudinite/local_packs/` sits *beside* `shared/`, which the submodule
   future outright requires — a submodule directory cannot carry the consumer's files.
2. **Minimal set, derived structurally from the declaration.** The vendor set is a function of
   `.claudinite-checks.json`, computed by [vendor.mjs](compute-vendor-set.mjs) with **no hand-maintained
   file list**: the one engine root (`engine/`) vendored wholesale, plus the **declared packs**
   with their `requires` closure — each pack's bundled skills riding its own directory (#385).
   There is no corpus-index `CLAUDE.md` and no consumer `@`-import: a session's rules arrive
   injected (#385). Excluded
   everywhere: tests; excluded at the engine root: `*.md` (canon-maintainer docs are read
   upstream when needed — a pack's `.md` files are the payload and ride their
   directories). Canon-internal trees (`docs/`, `.github/`, root maintainer docs)
   are never vendored. Two accepted edges: a newly declared pack has no local content until the
   next refresh (the engine's unknown-pack `config` error surfaces a declared-but-absent pack
   loudly), and links from vendored docs to non-vendored canon files may dangle locally by
   design (the sweep never inspects the shared mount — see 6).
3. **Preferences are never vendored** — per-user settings, not project content. The
   session-start step ([inject-preferences.sh](../engine/hooks/steps/inject-preferences.sh), mount machinery now)
   reads the local `preferences/<email>.md` when its tree carries one (the canon repo; a future
   submodule mount; the interim full-tarball sync) and otherwise **fetches just that file** over
   HTTPS, fresh each session. Every miss — no email, no file, fetch failure — is **fail-soft**:
   a one-line note and the session proceeds on defaults. The halt-gate is reserved for the
   load-bearing corpus, which after the flip is always local and can't miss.
4. **Transactional nightly update.** Per repo and per night: apply the pending migration notes,
   converge the vendored tree to the canon snapshot, advance the stamp — **one commit**. (One
   MCP reality: file *deletions* can't ride a `push_files` commit, so convergence's prunes
   follow as their own `delete_file` commits **after** the stamped content commit — safe to
   interrupt, since the next night's convergence re-deletes stragglers; note ops are
   stamp-gated and always land with the stamp — #329.) If the
   migration fails, nothing is written: the repo keeps running its old snapshot exactly as
   before, is retried the next night, and the failure lands in the fleet routine's failure log.
   The commit honors the repo's `maintenance.delivery` — both lanes land on the
   `claudinite/maintenance` branch and its PR (`auto-merge` arms auto-merge; `review` leaves it for the owner),
   never a direct commit to the default branch; each computes its writes against the *default*
   branch, drops what the maintenance branch already carries, and refreshes that branch from base
   each night — regenerate, never reconcile — #332. The refresh is
   **unconditional convergence** (copy-if-different, not copy-if-canon-moved), so an accidental
   local edit to a vendored file reverts within a day, visibly in the nightly's diff — that,
   plus a one-line "canon-owned; propose changes upstream" note, is the whole anti-drift story;
   there is deliberately no manifest/integrity framework. Direction-blindness cuts both ways,
   so the writer carries the one **anti-rewind guard** the no-framework stance leaves room for:
   converging is refused when the checkout's HEAD mismatches the passed ref or the member's
   stamped ref is not its ancestor, and the worker verifies the checkout is at the **remote**
   head before converging — a stale maintenance checkout must fail its unit, never silently
   downgrade the fleet (#328).
5. **The stamp.** `"claudinite": { "updated": "<full ISO datetime>", "ref": "<sha>" }` in
   `.claudinite-checks.json` — `updated` selects which migration notes still apply (notes are
   day-dated, so selection is by the stamp's **day, same-day inclusive** — a note landing later
   on the stamp's day must still apply, and note idempotency absorbs the re-application this
   admits — #330), `ref` is provenance for debugging **and** the anti-rewind guard's anchor (4). **One stamp for the whole set, never per pack**: updates are
   whole-set atomic, because mixed per-pack versions inside one repo would recreate exactly the
   engine↔pack skew this design eliminates (declaring a new pack therefore triggers a whole-set
   refresh, not a lone pack copy). The engine already tolerates the key
   (`CONFIG_KEYS` in engine/checks/helpers).
6. **The shared mount is structurally out of the sweep.** The engine's file-set builder drops
   everything under `.claudinite/shared/` (`buildContext` in engine/checks/helpers) — the corpus is
   canon-owned, never the project's own code — while `.claudinite/local_packs/` stays fully in
   scope. Deliberately a structural rule in the engine, **not** a `.gitattributes` /
   `linguist-vendored` convention: the exclusion must hold on any git host and any checkout.
   This is also what keeps the corpus-shape checks (catalog-completeness, skill-ownership)
   naturally inert in consumers with a pruned tree.
7. **Pinning semantics.** Each branch runs the snapshot committed on it: a session and its Stop
   hook judge by the same law, and a canon change affects no consumer until that
   consumer's own nightly commit. There is deliberately **no consumer CI workflow** (owner
   decision, #385): the Stop hook — which blocks the session from finishing until the sweep is
   green — is the enforcement surface, and an edit made outside Claude sessions surfaces at the
   next session's Stop sweep. Rollback is per-repo and atomic: revert the nightly's commit.
8. **Isolation.** Consumer files must not reference `.claudinite/` except the wiring set:
   `.claude/` (settings hook registrations),
   `.gitignore`, `.gitattributes`, `.github/workflows/` (a repo's own workflows may run the
   vendored engine), and anything under
   `.claudinite/` itself (`local_packs/` included). Product code that wants a canon helper
   inlines it — depending on canon internals would turn every canon refactor into a breaking
   migration for code the canon doesn't own. Enforced as a **fixed barrier the baseline pack
   contributes to the barriers mechanism pack** (manifest data under `contributes`; the baseline
   `requires` barriers, so the mechanism rides everywhere the baseline is declared) — the
   declaration-and-configuration composition pattern packs use with each other, never a
   cross-pack code import (the canon-side `pack-independence` barrier) — universal via the
   baseline, with no per-project barriers config to maintain; its `gateDir` keeps it inert
   until the vendored mount exists, so it fires neither in the canon repo nor in pre-flip
   consumers.
9. **Migration notes v2.** A canon change that consumers must be amended for ships as a dated
   record (the existing `migrations/active_migrations/` shape): mechanical ops where code can
   express them, plus a **brief agentic note** for what it can't (chiefly adapting
   consumer-authored `local_packs/` content to a changed engine contract). The nightly applies
   the notes dated on or after the day of the repo's stamp (same-day inclusive, note
   idempotency absorbing the overlap — #330), oldest first, inside the one transactional commit.
   No read-side tolerances in live code, no `LEGACY_*` constants, and **no per-consumer state
   held in the canon** — the stamp in each consumer is the only bookkeeping. **Retirement is a
   retention window**: a note is deleted ~5 weeks after landing; a repo lagging longer has been
   failing loudly in the nightly log (or was off the access list), and its catch-up path is
   re-running adoption, which vendors head idempotently. The one surviving two-phase case is
   **out-of-repo state** no commit can reach — the pasted web-environment Setup script keeps
   the probe + halt-gate pattern ([consumer-safe-changes.md](../consumer-safe-changes.md)).
10. **Accepted trade-off.** A bad canon change (typically an overzealous blocking check)
    reaches consumers on one nightly and its fix on a later one — up to ~two days' exposure.
    Dampers: the Stop hook's own two-block self-release, per-repo `rules`/`accept` overrides,
    and an on-demand refresh (the nightly's update step run in-session) as the
    pull-forward/emergency lane.

**What this retires:** the per-session fetch and its halt-gate, the `codeload.github.com`
allowlist prerequisite, `CLAUDINITE_REF` pinning (the commit *is* the pin), the
`.claudinite.new` swap and tracked-copy preservation, the Method A/B split with the submodule
caveats, and the stale-mount caveat in [engine/checks/README.md](../engine/checks/README.md). Session start
becomes a single offline SessionStart entry invoking [session-start.sh](../engine/hooks/session-start-command.sh)
directly (its four steps are unchanged; the preferences step is fail-soft per 3, the env-check
halt-gate stays). The consumer `CLAUDE.md` carries nothing of Claudinite's — the corpus
index, its `@`-import, and the self-check paragraph are all retired by owner decision (#385). The
plugin-packaging rationale in [engine/checks/DESIGN.md](../engine/checks/DESIGN.md) also loses its
update-latency premise — recorded there when the transition completes. The canon repo itself is
untouched: it runs its own live tree and mounts nothing.

the nightly touches everyone, and never break the channel the migration itself travels through.

## The vendor-set contract ([vendor.mjs](compute-vendor-set.mjs))

`computeVendorSet(declaredEntries)` → `{ files, errors }`, computed against the
canon tree the module ships in; the writer materializes `files` under `SHARED_SUBDIR`
(exported; defined beside `LOCAL_PACKS_SUBDIR` in the packs registry). Structural throughout:
`ENGINE_DIR_ROOTS` walks (tests and root-docs excluded), `MACHINERY_ROOTS` top-level `.mjs`,
resolved canon packs' directories (each pack's bundled skills riding its own tree — #385) —
never a per-file list. Declared ids that
name no canon pack (a consumer's local packs, or a typo the runner's settings validation
already flags) are skipped without error. The computed set is verified
**import-closed** before it is returned: a vendored module whose relative
import resolves outside the set (or to nothing) is reported in `errors`, so
convergence aborts before any write instead of a flipped member crashing on a
missing module — the guard is judged against the same engine-surface
definitions the `pack-independence` barrier confines pack imports to (one home,

{"number":567,"title":"Preferences belong to the fleet: a declared home, and the sheepdog sweep that names it","body":"Personal interaction preferences are the concern of **one fleet's users**. The canon is mounted by every fleet that adopts Claudinite, which makes it both the wrong host for one owner's preferences and the wrong authority on where they live — yet `preferences/.md` sat here, and the session-start step fell back to a hardcoded `raw.githubusercontent.com/[REDACTED:env:CCR_TRIGGER_REPO]/main/preferences` URL.

So the canon stops holding them and starts **asking**. Two commits, each standing alone.

## 1 — the declared home (the capability)

A project names the home in its own settings; the session-start step resolves it:

```json
"preferences": { "repo": "owner/fleet-repo", "path": "preferences" }
```

- `path` defaults to `preferences`, and the whole key is **optional** — a project with no fleet behind it has no preferences home, and that is an ordinary state, not a fault. A *declared* pointer that doesn't resolve **is** a settings error: it claims a home while the session quietly gets defaults, and a preference nobody sees is indistinguishable from one nobody wrote.
- `preferencesLocation` is the one resolver, exported for a **raw** declaration as well as a loaded config — the `isDormant` contract, for the same reason: a cross-repo reader has no engine loaded against the tree it is reading, and must resolve a pointer by the same test the session-start step used.
- The step becomes `engine/hooks/steps/inject-preferences.mjs` (was `.sh`) — reading one key out of a JSON declaration in bash meant either parsing JSON there or shelling out to node anyway. Same **fail-soft** contract: every miss is one plain-text line and the session proceeds on defaults, never a halt directive. Local-first now resolves against the **project** dir at the declared path, so the preferences home repo reads its own working copy rather than its default branch. An implausible email is refused rather than traversed with.
- `preferences/[REDACTED:env:CLAUDE_CODE_USER_EMAIL].md` moves to **missingbulb/Sheepdog** (missingbulb/Sheepdog#35), and this repo's declaration points there.

Bootstrap deliberately does **not** populate the pointer: a run from canon doesn't know which fleet it is bootstrapping into, and hardcoding one fleet's repo in shared code is the coupling this removes.

## 2 — the sheepdog pack's fourth sweep (who populates it)

`fleet-preferences` (daily, agentless, the sweep as its preprocessing — the same shape as the other three) reads every covered member's declaration and writes the pointer into the ones that lack it. Its home is `preferencesRepo` on the sheepdog pack entry's `config`, defaulting to the **enforcer repo itself**; a fleet keeping preferences elsewhere names it there.

This is the **one** sweep in the pack that writes to a member, and the **one** write primitive in `fleet-api` (`putFile`), so "what can this change in someone else's repo" has a single answer to read. It stays narrow: one additive settings key, one PUT to the default branch guarded by the blob sha the read returned, idempotent, no issue in either direction. The census and freshness sweeps converge issues because their findings need a human; the fleet's preferences home is a fact this repo holds, so an issue asking someone to copy it into every member would be ceremony around a mechanical edit.

Three rules carry it:

| | |
|---|---|
| **the engine gate** | An unknown top-level setting is a blocking `config` error, and a member runs whatever engine its vendored mount carries. The sweep reads the member's **own** engine and writes only when that file's `CONFIG_KEYS` names the key. Reading the vocabulary itself — not a version, not a date — is what makes the rollout need no coordination: members re-vendor nightly and are written the first run after their own mount learned the key. `engine-behind` is a **wait**, not a finding. |
| **a pointer at another repo is a decision** | Reported, never overwritten. |
| **a dormant member is skipped** | A commit landed from outside is exactly the upkeep it opted out of. |

## What the owner has to do

**The `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN` PAT needs Contents *write* across the owner's repos** (it was Metadata + Contents read, Issues read/write). Until it does, the sweep fails loudly and the scheduler converges a `needs-human` issue — by design, rather than leaving members quietly unpointed.

## Rollout, and why no other member's declaration is edited here

Only this repo's declaration gets the key in this PR. Every other member's vendored engine still predates the setting, so writing it by hand today would be a blocking `config` error in that repo until its next baselining. The gate is what makes the rollout safe: canon lands → members re-vendor nightly → the daily sweep writes each one the morning after its own mount learned the key. Sheepdog's own declaration is written by that same sweep, which also proves the mechanism end to end.

## Verification

- Full suite: **989 tests, 0 failures**. World sweep: **0 blocking** (one new advisory `file-placement`, the step's reach for the shared resolver — the same distance-3/4 family the `engine/scheduler/` modules already sit in; duplicating the resolver is the thing this design exists to avoid).
- New tests: the pointer resolver and its settings errors, the step's three fail-soft paths and the local-first win, `putFile`'s sha guard and scope-naming errors, every branch of the sweep's classification, and the edit's idempotence. The engine gate's test reads **this repo's** engine source, so renaming `CONFIG_KEYS` past the pattern fails there instead of silently answering "no" for every member forever.
- Live check against Sheepdog's branch: the step fetches the real file end to end, and both URL forms it builds resolve (`HEAD` as a ref, and the percent-encoded `@` in the filename).
- The vendor set stays import-closed and carries the new step and task; the scheduler discovers `fleet-preferences` with no errors.

[{"number":569,"title":"Pack manifests as JSON: pack.json + pack.schema.json, code split into sibling files","body":"Closes #564.

A pack declared itself in a `pack.mjs` module, so **discovering** a pack meant **executing** one — at every session start and every check run, in every consumer, over their hand-written local packs too. Almost none of that code was doing anything: across the 29 manifests, 56 of 988 lines were `import` statements naming rule modules, and most of the rest was data.

The manifest is now `packs//pack.json` (**498 lines** across all 29, down from 988), with the code a pack genuinely needs in siblings the JSON names by filename. **Twenty-four of the twenty-nine execute nothing at load** beyond the rule modules they were always going to import.

## The shape

```json
{
  "$schema": "../../engine/pack_loader/pack.schema.json",
  "id": "python",
  "ruleRoutingGuidance": { "belongs": "…", "excludes": "…" },
  "marker": "pyproject.toml (at the repo root or one directory down)",
  "detect": { "trackedPath": { "basename": "pyproject.toml", "maxDepth": 2 } },
  "prose": "RULES.md",
  "skills": ["python-optional-deps"]
}
```

- **`engine/pack_loader/pack.schema.json`** is the authoring spec — a real JSON Schema, so an editor validates and completes a manifest while you type it, and the loader validates against the same document.
- **`json-schema.mjs`** implements exactly the keywords that schema uses and reports any other as a *schema fault*. A validator that silently skipped `oneOf` would let a future schema edit look enforced while enforcing nothing; `unsupportedKeywords()` audits the live schema in CI so the gap is caught before it ships. (No dependency: the engine is dependency-free and reachable from every consumer's SessionStart hook.)
- **`detect-spec.mjs`** compiles the fingerprint most packs need from data — `is` / `endsWith` / `basename` / `matches` / `maxDepth`, all of which must hold of the *same* tracked path. Ten packs' one-line arrow functions became one line of JSON each.
- **Code only where a pack has some**: `detect.mjs` in the 4 packs whose fingerprint reads file *content* (chrome-extension, chrome-extension-release, leaflet, web-speech), `env.mjs` in the 1 whose shell is a function of project config (node), `contributed.mjs` as the barriers seam. Flutter's `env` stayed inline — the schema takes a line list and joins it, so a multi-line install still reads as lines.

## The guard the filename shape buys

Rules arrive as filenames, so the loader can hold the manifest and the directory to each other: **every `.mjs` at the pack root must be accounted for** — a rule in exactly one scope list, a module some other field names, or a declared `helpers` entry. Before this, a rule module nobody added to the manifest sat in the pack, read as "a check", and ran nowhere.

## Two sources of shape, one drift guard

`pack.schema.json` owns the **JSON**; `PACK_FIELDS` in `pack-schema.mjs` now owns the **resolved in-memory manifest** (and the legacy `pack.mjs` shape while it lasts), alongside the guards no schema can state — the 20-word routing cap, a rule's `scope` agreeing with its list, skills vs the tree. A test asserts the two vocabularies name the same fields and agree on which are required, so they cannot drift.

## Consumer safety

`pack.mjs` is a **consumer-held** shape — every member repo authors its own local packs — so per `consumer-safe-changes.md`:

- the registry reads **either** manifest, prefers `pack.json` where both exist (a half-finished migration must not resolve to the old shape), reports the leftover module for deletion, and stamps `manifestFile` so a finding names the file the consumer actually has;
- the `pack-json-manifest` baseline migration carries the per-repo conversion (agentic — what a `detect` closure must become depends on what it does) and its `legacyPresent` telemetry says when the fleet has finished. `retire: 'manual'`, because the tolerance is inline in the registry.

Two readers that scanned for `pack.mjs` also got *simpler*: the home's `seededByDefault` audit and the pack-prose narration rule now `JSON.parse` the manifest instead of pattern-matching module source past a hand-rolled comment stripper — which is what both rules claimed to be doing all along.

## The 350 comment lines

Most turned out to be already housed in the pack's README, which is what #559 made that file for. What was genuinely only in a comment landed there — `basics`'s composition (why it `requires` barriers and *contributes* the isolation wall as data), product-wiki's and executable-requirements' interview rationale, chrome-extension-release's on-demand RELEASE.md, firebase's relevance-first guards — and four stub packs plus the home's `claudinite` local pack got a README at all. The near-root `maxDepth: 2` idiom was the same paragraph in four manifests, so it lands once, beside the matcher it explains.

## Verification

- **1004 tests pass** (was 965; +39 across `json-schema`, `detect-spec`, `pack-json`, the vocabulary drift guard, and both-shapes tolerance), **0 blocking conformance findings**.
- `engine-tests/pack-detect.test.mjs` is the end-to-end proof that the compiled `{ basename, maxDepth: 2 }` spec means exactly what the three arrow functions it replaced meant — at the root, one directory down, never deeper, basename only.
- `pack-json.test.mjs` runs the accounted-for and `$schema`-pointer guards over the **real corpus**, and holds all 29 manifests to one field order (the schema's own, so there is no second list to drift).
- The vendoring and pack-loader test fixtures stopped enumerating the loader's modules and copy `engine/pack_loader/` wholesale — the fixture going stale the next time the loader gains a file is exactly how this change first broke them.

The canon is mounted by every fleet that adopts Claudinite, which makes it both the wrong host for one owner's preferences and the wrong authority on where they live — yet `preferences/.md` sat here, and the session-start step fell back to a hardcoded `raw.githubusercontent.com/[REDACTED:env:CCR_TRIGGER_REPO]/main/preferences` URL.

So the canon stops holding them and starts **asking**. Two commits, each standing alone.

## 1 — the declared home (the capability)

A project names the home in its own settings; the session-start step resolves it:

```json
"preferences": { "repo": "owner/fleet-repo", "path": "preferences" }
```

- `path` defaults to `preferences`, and the whole key is **optional** — a project with no fleet behind it has no preferences home, and that is an ordinary state, not a fault. A *declared* pointer that doesn't resolve **is** a settings error: it claims a home while the session quietly gets defaults, and a preference nobody sees is indistinguishable from one nobody wrote.
- `preferencesLocation` is the one resolver, exported for a **raw** declaration as well as a loaded config — the `isDormant` contract, for the same reason: a cross-repo reader has no engine loaded against the tree it is reading, and must resolve a pointer by the same test the session-start step used.
- The step becomes `engine/hooks/steps/inject-preferences.mjs` (was `.sh`) — reading one key out of a JSON declaration in bash meant either parsing JSON there or shelling out to node anyway. Same **fail-soft** contract: every miss is one plain-text line and the session proceeds on defaults, never a halt directive. Local-first now resolves against the **project** dir at the declared path, so the preferences home repo reads its own working copy rather than its default branch. An implausible email is refused rather than traversed with.
- `preferences/[REDACTED:env:CLAUDE_CODE_USER_EMAIL].md` moves to **missingbulb/Sheepdog** (missingbulb/Sheepdog#35), and this repo's declaration points there.

Bootstrap deliberately does **not** populate the pointer: a run from canon doesn't know which fleet it is bootstrapping into, and hardcoding one fleet's repo in shared code is the coupling this removes.

## 2 — the sheepdog pack's fourth sweep (who populates it)

`fleet-preferences` (daily, agentless, the sweep as its preprocessing — the same shape as the other three) reads every covered member's declaration and writes the pointer into the ones that lack it. Its home is `preferencesRepo` on the sheepdog pack entry's `config`, defaulting to the **enforcer repo itself**; a fleet keeping preferences elsewhere names it there.

This is the **one** sweep in the pack that writes to a member, and the **one** write primitive in `fleet-api` (`putFile`), so "what can this change in someone else's repo" has a single answer to read. It stays narrow: one additive settings key, one PUT to the default branch guarded by the blob sha the read returned, idempotent, no issue in either direction. The census and freshness sweeps converge issues because their findings need a human; the fleet's preferences home is a fact this repo holds, so an issue asking someone to copy it into every member would be ceremony around a mechanical edit.

Three rules carry it:

| | |
|---|---|
| **the engine gate** | An unknown top-level setting is a blocking `config` error, and a member runs whatever engine its vendored mount carries. The sweep reads the member's **own** engine and writes only when that file's `CONFIG_KEYS` names the key. Reading the vocabulary itself — not a version, not a date — is what makes the rollout need no coordination: members re-vendor nightly and are written the first run after their own mount learned the key. `engine-behind` is a **wait**, not a finding. |
| **a pointer at another repo is a decision** | Reported, never overwritten. |
| **a dormant member is skipped** | A commit landed from outside is exactly the upkeep it opted out of. |

## What the owner has to do

**The `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN` PAT needs Contents *write* across the owner's repos** (it was Metadata + Contents read, Issues read/write). Until it does, the sweep fails loudly and the scheduler converges a `needs-human` issue — by design, rather than leaving members quietly unpointed.

## Rollout, and why no other member's declaration is edited here

Only this repo's declaration gets the key in this PR. Every other member's vendored engine still predates the setting, so writing it by hand today would be a blocking `config` error in that repo until its next baselining. The gate is what makes the rollout safe: canon lands → members re-vendor nightly → the daily sweep writes each one the morning after its own mount learned the key. Sheepdog's own declaration is written by that same sweep, which also proves the mechanism end to end.

## Verification

- Full suite: **989 tests, 0 failures**. World sweep: **0 blocking** (one new advisory `file-placement`, the step's reach for the shared resolver — the same distance-3/4 family the `engine/scheduler/` modules already sit in; duplicating the resolver is the thing this design exists to avoid).
- New tests: the pointer resolver and its settings errors, the step's three fail-soft paths and the local-first win, `putFile`'s sha guard and scope-naming errors, every branch of the sweep's classification, and the edit's idempotence. The engine gate's test reads **this repo's** engine source, so renaming `CONFIG_KEYS` past the pattern fails there instead of silently answering "no" for every member forever.
- Live check against Sheepdog's branch: the step fetches the real file end to end, and both URL forms it builds resolve (`HEAD` as a ref, and the percent-encoded `@` in the filename).
- The vendor set stays import-closed and carries the new step and task; the scheduler discovers `fleet-preferences` with no errors.

## What this does

**Tasks now work through skills.** Following the existing `prose-to-checks` (skill) / `prose-to-checks-sweep` (task) split:

- `packs/grow_with_claudinite/skills/growth-extract/SKILL.md` — the capture method: the durable/reusable bar, dedupe against the corpus and check catalog, capture at the repo's own level, the local promotion ladder (check > pack skill > prose).
- `packs/grow_with_claudinite/skills/growth-dedup/SKILL.md` — the prune method: the mounted-canon yardstick, remove/strip/rephrase (every action removes portable text), the keep-test (says *more*, not merely more specifically), checks-count-as-coverage.
- Each `task.md` slims to the unattended-run framing (executor dispatch, Context scope, PR/auto-merge mechanics, tracking issue, model) and delegates the method: "The method lives in the skill." Skills are also invocable in-session for owner-requested capture/reconcile work.

**A write-surface check gates the runs.** New `growth-write-scope` (blocking, work scope, registered on `grow_with_claudinite`): both task docs pin commit titles (`Claudinite growth: extract lessons` / `Claudinite growth: dedup local packs`), and when a branch carries a `Claudinite growth:`-prefixed commit subject, **every touched path — added, modified, or deleted — must sit under `.claudinite/local/packs/`** (legacy `.claudinite/local_packs/` accepted during the rename window). Owner call: a growth run has one responsibility — improving the repo's packs with rules, checks, and skills — never the repo's codebase, comments included; a site-tied gotcha lands as the owning pack's entry naming the site. (An intermediate revision allowed comment-line insertions outside the packs; commits `a5027c2` / its revert record that exploration.)

[{"number":569,"title":"Pack manifests as JSON: pack.json + pack.schema.json, code split into sibling files","body":"Closes #564.

A pack declared itself in a `pack.mjs` module, so **discovering** a pack meant **executing** one — at every session start and every check run, in every consumer, over their hand-written local packs too. Almost none of that code was doing anything: across the 29 manifests, 56 of 988 lines were `import` statements naming rule modules, and most of the rest was data.

The manifest is now `packs//pack.json` (**498 lines** across all 29, down from 988), with the code a pack genuinely needs in siblings the JSON names by filename. **Twenty-four of the twenty-nine execute nothing at load** beyond the rule modules they were always going to import.

## The shape

```json
{
  "$schema": "../../engine/pack_loader/pack.schema.json",
  "id": "python",
  "ruleRoutingGuidance": { "belongs": "…", "excludes": "…" },
  "marker": "pyproject.toml (at the repo root or one directory down)",
  "detect": { "trackedPath": { "basename": "pyproject.toml", "maxDepth": 2 } },
  "prose": "RULES.md",
  "skills": ["python-optional-deps"]
}
```

- **`engine/pack_loader/pack.schema.json`** is the authoring spec — a real JSON Schema, so an editor validates and completes a manifest while you type it, and the loader validates against the same document.
- **`json-schema.mjs`** implements exactly the keywords that schema uses and reports any other as a *schema fault*. A validator that silently skipped `oneOf` would let a future schema edit look enforced while enforcing nothing; `unsupportedKeywords()` audits the live schema in CI so the gap is caught before it ships. (No dependency: the engine is dependency-free and reachable from every consumer's SessionStart hook.)
- **`detect-spec.mjs`** compiles the fingerprint most packs need from data — `is` / `endsWith` / `basename` / `matches` / `maxDepth`, all of which must hold of the *same* tracked path. Ten packs' one-line arrow functions became one line of JSON each.
- **Code only where a pack has some**: `detect.mjs` in the 4 packs whose fingerprint reads file *content* (chrome-extension, chrome-extension-release, leaflet, web-speech), `env.mjs` in the 1 whose shell is a function of project config (node), `contributed.mjs` as the barriers seam. Flutter's `env` stayed inline — the schema takes a line list and joins it, so a multi-line install still reads as lines.

## The guard the filename shape buys

Rules arrive as filenames, so the loader can hold the manifest and the directory to each other: **every `.mjs` at the pack root must be accounted for** — a rule in exactly one scope list, a module some other field names, or a declared `helpers` entry. Before this, a rule module nobody added to the manifest sat in the pack, read as "a check", and ran nowhere.

## Two sources of shape, one drift guard

`pack.schema.json` owns the **JSON**; `PACK_FIELDS` in `pack-schema.mjs` now owns the **resolved in-memory manifest** (and the legacy `pack.mjs` shape while it lasts), alongside the guards no schema can state — the 20-word routing cap, a rule's `scope` agreeing with its list, skills vs the tree. A test asserts the two vocabularies name the same fields and agree on which are required, so they cannot drift.

## Consumer safety

`pack.mjs` is a **consumer-held** shape — every member repo authors its own local packs — so per `consumer-safe-changes.md`:

- the registry reads **either** manifest, prefers `pack.json` where both exist (a half-finished migration must not resolve to the old shape), reports the leftover module for deletion, and stamps `manifestFile` so a finding names the file the consumer actually has;
- the `pack-json-manifest` baseline migration carries the per-repo conversion (agentic — what a `detect` closure must become depends on what it does) and its `legacyPresent` telemetry says when the fleet has finished. `retire: 'manual'`, because the tolerance is inline in the registry.

Two readers that scanned for `pack.mjs` also got *simpler*: the home's `seededByDefault` audit and the pack-prose narration rule now `JSON.parse` the manifest instead of pattern-matching module source past a hand-rolled comment stripper — which is what both rules claimed to be doing all along.

## The 350 comment lines

Most turned out to be already housed in the pack's README, which is what #559 made that file for. What was genuinely only in a comment landed there — `basics`'s composition (why it `requires` barriers and *contributes* the isolation wall as data), product-wiki's and executable-requirements' interview rationale, chrome-extension-release's on-demand RELEASE.md, firebase's relevance-first guards — and four stub packs plus the home's `claudinite` local pack got a README at all. The near-root `maxDepth: 2` idiom was the same paragraph in four manifests, so it lands once, beside the matcher it explains.

## Verification

- **1004 tests pass** (was 965; +39 across `json-schema`, `detect-spec`, `pack-json`, the vocabulary drift guard, and both-shapes tolerance), **0 blocking conformance findings**.
- `engine-tests/pack-detect.test.mjs` is the end-to-end proof that the compiled `{ basename, maxDepth: 2 }` spec means exactly what the three arrow functions it replaced meant — at the root, one directory down, never deeper, basename only.
- `pack-json.test.mjs` runs the accounted-for and `$schema`-pointer guards over the **real corpus**, and holds all 29 manifests to one field order (the schema's own, so there is no second list to drift).
- The vendoring and pack-loader test fixtures stopped enumerating the loader's modules and copy `engine/pack_loader/` wholesale — the fixture going stale the next time the loader gains a file is exactly how this change first broke them.

So the canon stops holding them and starts **asking**. Two commits, each standing alone.

## 1 — the declared home (the capability)

A project names the home in its own settings; the session-start step resolves it:

```json
"preferences": { "repo": "owner/fleet-repo", "path": "preferences" }
```

- `path` defaults to `preferences`, and the whole key is **optional** — a project with no fleet behind it has no preferences home, and that is an ordinary state, not a fault. A *declared* pointer that doesn't resolve **is** a settings error: it claims a home while the session quietly gets defaults, and a preference nobody sees is indistinguishable from one nobody wrote.
- `preferencesLocation` is the one resolver, exported for a **raw** declaration as well as a loaded config — the `isDormant` contract, for the same reason: a cross-repo reader has no engine loaded against the tree it is reading, and must resolve a pointer by the same test the session-start step used.
- The step becomes `engine/hooks/steps/inject-preferences.mjs` (was `.sh`) — reading one key out of a JSON declaration in bash meant either parsing JSON there or shelling out to node anyway. Same **fail-soft** contract: every miss is one plain-text line and the session proceeds on defaults, never a halt directive. Local-first now resolves against the **project** dir at the declared path, so the preferences home repo reads its own working copy rather than its default branch. An implausible email is refused rather than traversed with.
- `preferences/[REDACTED:env:CLAUDE_CODE_USER_EMAIL].md` moves to **missingbulb/Sheepdog** (missingbulb/Sheepdog#35), and this repo's declaration points there.

Bootstrap deliberately does **not** populate the pointer: a run from canon doesn't know which fleet it is bootstrapping into, and hardcoding one fleet's repo in shared code is the coupling this removes.

## 2 — the sheepdog pack's fourth sweep (who populates it)

`fleet-preferences` (daily, agentless, the sweep as its preprocessing — the same shape as the other three) reads every covered member's declaration and writes the pointer into the ones that lack it. Its home is `preferencesRepo` on the sheepdog pack entry's `config`, defaulting to the **enforcer repo itself**; a fleet keeping preferences elsewhere names it there.

This is the **one** sweep in the pack that writes to a member, and the **one** write primitive in `fleet-api` (`putFile`), so "what can this change in someone else's repo" has a single answer to read. It stays narrow: one additive settings key, one PUT to the default branch guarded by the blob sha the read returned, idempotent, no issue in either direction. The census and freshness sweeps converge issues because their findings need a human; the fleet's preferences home is a fact this repo holds, so an issue asking someone to copy it into every member would be ceremony around a mechanical edit.

| **a dormant member is skipped** | A commit landed from outside is exactly the upkeep it opted out of. |

Only this repo's declaration gets the key in this PR. Every other member's vendored engine still predates the setting, so writing it by hand today would be a blocking `config` error in that repo until its next baselining.
